name: UK inflation & rates
summary: Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov; CPI 3.5% in September, expected near 5% by mid-2027
state: UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in the 12 months to September, up from 3.1% in August and inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band (ONS, 21 Oct). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate by 0.25 points to 4% in a decision published on 5 Nov, on an 8–1 vote with one member favouring 4.25%. The Bank expects CPI of about 5% by mid-2027 as energy costs feed through. October CPI is due on 18 Nov.
for_you: Households on variable-rate or tracker mortgages and those with deals ending soon are most exposed to the higher Bank Rate. Rising prices weigh most on lower-income households.
rubric_hit: Watch: CPI 3.5% within 2.5–4.0% band, and BoE reversing course with a rise to 4%. Alert line (CPI above 4.0% or an emergency move) not met.
